name: Human Resources Specialist
description: Human resources specialists recruit and hire, administer pay and benefits, interpret employment law and policy, and handle the disputes and complaints that come with employing people. ⚠ A median of $75,940 across 939,700 jobs, all of it growing. ⚠⚠ It is the most open CHOICE path on this site: business supplies only about a quarter of HR workers, PSYCHOLOGY is the second largest feeder, and 16% have no degree beyond some college. ⚠⚠⚠ And the money is in progression, not credentials — the step to HR manager is worth $73,340 and asks for experience, not another degree.
credentialNote: ⚠ No licence, no board, no state examination — Florida does not regulate this work and neither does any other state. What exists instead is voluntary professional certification: the BLS notes that associations offer certification programmes requiring an examination plus minimum education and experience, and that while certification is usually voluntary, some employers prefer or require it. ⚠⚠ Read that ordering carefully, because it is unusual: the certifications here generally require EXPERIENCE as well as study, so they are mid-career credentials rather than entry tickets. You cannot certify your way into a first HR job the way you can into a first networking job. ⚠⚠⚠ What the field actually gates on is employment law. An HR specialist who misapplies the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act or Title VII exposes the employer to real liability — which is why the courses that matter most in this list are the law ones, and why judgement and documentation habits matter more than any credential.
bodyHtml:
Four roles, and all of them are growing

This page covers the human resources family, because the degrees are shared and people move between the roles. Unlike the financial and networking families on this site, nothing here is contracting.

RoleSOC2025 medianJobsOutlook 2025–35
Training and development specialist13-1151$69,280472,500✅✅ 11% much faster
Human resources specialist13-1071$75,940939,700✅ 6% faster
Compensation, benefits and job analysis specialist13-1141$78,210118,100✅ 6% faster
Human resources manager11-3121⚠⚠ $149,280224,9006% faster, 5+ years' experience

⚠⚠⚠ Look at the last row. The step from specialist to manager is worth $73,340 — nearly doubling the median, and the largest single ladder step measured anywhere on this site. What it asks for is five years or more of related experience, not another degree.

⚠ That should change how you plan. In most careers here the money question is which credential to buy; in this one it is how quickly you can get into the field and start accumulating the experience that the manager role requires. Training and development is the fastest-growing entry point at 11% and 472,500 jobs, and it pays least — which makes it a good door rather than a good destination.

What the work actually is

O*NET, on human resources specialists: interpret and explain human resources policies, procedures, laws, standards, or regulations; hire employees and process hiring-related paperwork; maintain current knowledge of Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and affirmative action guidelines and laws; prepare or maintain employment records related to events, such as hiring, termination, leaves, transfers, or promotions; address employee relations issues, such as harassment allegations, work complaints, or other employee concerns.

⚠⚠ Two of those five are law and one is conflict. The recruiting half is what attracts people to HR; the compliance and employee-relations half is what the job mostly is, and it is the half that carries consequences. If handling a harassment allegation properly, in writing, under pressure, sounds like the wrong kind of hard, this is the wrong career.

⚠⚠⚠ The most open CHOICE path on this site

Census American Community Survey microdata, reported through Data USA for 2024, counts degrees held by 1,016,447 human resources workers:

Field of degreePeopleRoughly
Business250,30325%
⚠ Psychology62,6396%
Social sciences55,1345%

⚠⚠ Compare the top row across the CHOICE paths on this site. For financial analysts, business supplies about half. For software developers, computing supplies under a third. Here the largest field supplies a quarter, and the three named fields together account for barely a third of the occupation — so roughly two thirds of HR workers studied something else entirely.

⚠⚠⚠ Psychology being second is the finding worth acting on. There are not many well-paid business careers where a psychology degree is a mainstream route rather than a detour, and this is one — the subject matter is selection, motivation, behaviour and conflict. If you are a psychology student wondering what the degree leads to besides graduate school, this is a real answer.

⚠ And the degree bar is lower than in the rest of the business cluster: of the same population, 460,579 hold a bachelor's, 192,446 a graduate degree, and 167,046 have some college and no degree — about 16%. O*NET's respondents name a bachelor's at only 47%. This is an occupation people enter sideways, from administration, operations and the shop floor, and the data shows it.

⚠⚠ The source's own caution: Data USA counts all academic degrees rather than one per person, and ACS records a field of degree only for bachelor's holders. Read the proportions, not the head counts.

⚠⚠ Florida barely teaches this as a degree — and that is fine

If you go looking for a human resources major in Florida you will mostly not find one. Exactly one public institution in the state — Florida International University — awards degrees under the human resources CIP code, producing about 300 a year.

⚠⚠⚠ What Florida has instead is business administration at 46 public institutions and roughly 19,500 credentials a year, with human resources as a concentration inside it. That is not a gap; it is how the field is taught, and it matches the entrant data — a quarter of HR workers hold a business degree and hardly any hold an HR degree, because hardly any exist.

⚠ So the practical route is: a business administration degree with an HR concentration, or a psychology degree with employment-law and management courses bolted on. Both are well supported in Florida, and the second is the one nobody tells psychology students about.

✅ The courses travel well, with one number to watch

The core HR courses are unusually widely carried for upper-division business subjects: MAN 4301 Human Resource Management at 23 institutions, MAN 3240 Organizational Behavior at 29, MAN 4320 Recruitment and Selection at 12, MAN 4350 Training and Development at 11. The lower division is the standard business core, which travels better than almost anything on this site.

⚠⚠ The one trap is the same shape as finance's. Human resource management is carried under two numbers: MAN 4301 at 23 institutions and MAN 3301 at 10 — and they sit at different levels, 4000 against 3000. Same subject, and a requirement check matches on the number. Ask which one your degree audit expects.

⚠ One more worth knowing about: MAN 4350 Training and Development and MAN 4320 Recruitment and Selection are the two courses aimed directly at the fastest-growing and the most-hiring parts of this family respectively. They are electives at most institutions. Take both.

Necessary skills

  • Employment law, applied. FLSA, FMLA, ADA, Title VII and Florida's own provisions. This is the part with legal consequences and the part employers pay for.
  • Documentation discipline. In a dispute, what happened is what the file says happened. HR people who write contemporaneous, neutral records win; the others lose.
  • Conflict handling without taking sides prematurely. Investigations require you to be the person who has not decided yet.
  • Confidentiality under pressure, including from managers who outrank you and want to know.
  • Data fluency. Compensation analysis, turnover metrics and pay-equity review are the analytical half of the field and the route to the better-paid specialisms.
  • Plain writing. Policies people actually follow are policies people can read.

Advice

⚠⚠ Stop looking for an HR degree and take business administration with an HR concentration — or psychology with employment law and management alongside. One Florida public institution awards the HR degree; 46 award the business one.

⚠ Get in early and count the years. The manager step is worth $73,340 and asks for five years of experience. That makes an internship, a coordinator job or an HR assistant role in your final year worth more than an extra credential.

⚠ Do not buy certification as a student. The main HR certifications require experience as well as study, so they are mid-career credentials. Plan for one at the three-to-five-year mark, when it will actually change what you are paid.

⚠ Take the employment law courses seriously, even the dull ones. The judgement calls in this job are legal judgement calls, and the cost of getting one wrong lands on your employer and then on you.

And if you are studying psychology, know that this field is genuinely open to you. Psychology is the second largest feeder into HR nationally, ahead of every other non-business field. Add employment law, organisational behaviour and a statistics course, and you are a credible candidate rather than a career-changer.

cipCodes.note: Business administration, management and operations — 46 Florida public institutions and roughly 19,500 credentials, the largest programme footprint in the state, and where human resources is actually taught as a concentration. ⚠ Business supplies about a quarter of working HR staff, the largest single field.

⚠ Psychology — the SECOND largest feeder into this occupation nationally at about 6% of HR workers, ahead of every other non-business field. Selection, motivation, behaviour and conflict are the subject matter, and this is one of the few well-paid business destinations where a psychology degree is a mainstream route.

Social sciences — about 5% of HR workers, the third named field. Included because the counted data shows roughly two thirds of this occupation studied outside business, and the social sciences are a substantial part of that remainder.

programs.note: The actual route in Florida, and the one to take: 46 public institutions against a single one awarding a human resources degree. ⚠ Read its degrees note — the breadth is the strength and the weakness, so what distinguishes you is the HR concentration, the employment-law courses and the internships taken inside it.

⚠ Not a route here, but named because compensation, benefits and job analysis is the best-paid specialist rung in this family and it is quantitative work. ⚠⚠ An HR professional who can genuinely analyse pay data is scarce — accounting or statistics coursework alongside a business degree is what produces one.

⚠ Not a route here. Named because benefits and compensation design is financial work, and because the two degrees compete for the same students — finance is narrower, more quantitative and taught at 12 institutions; business administration is broader and at 46.

courses.reason: Human Resource Management — 23 institutions, the core course of this career and the most widely carried HR subject in the state. Staffing, appraisal, compensation, employment law and labour relations in one survey.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Florida carries this subject under TWO numbers at DIFFERENT levels: MAN4301 at 23 institutions and MAN3301 at 10. Same subject, 4000 against 3000, and a degree audit matches on the number. ⚠ Ask which your programme expects before taking either.

courses.reason: Human Resource Management — 10 institutions, the 3000-level version of the same core course. Listed so the split is visible from both sides.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Not a lesser course — a different number. It is the one FGCU, UCF, USF, UWF and several state colleges use.

courses.reason: Organizational Behavior — 29 institutions, the most widely carried upper-division management course in Florida. Motivation, groups, leadership and why people at work do what they do.
courses.variantNote: ✅ Widely carried and widely accepted. It is also the course closest to the psychology route into this field.

courses.reason: Recruitment and Selection — 12 institutions. The hiring half of the job done properly: job analysis, valid selection methods and the legal constraints on both.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ An elective at most institutions and the one aimed at the largest part of the occupation. Take it. ⚠⚠ Note that this prefix carries a documented subject collision — some institutions teach recruitment under MAN4350 and training under MAN4320 — so read the description rather than the title.

courses.reason: Training and Development — 11 institutions. Aimed at the fastest-growing role in this family: training and development specialists, 11% growth and 472,500 jobs.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also an elective at most institutions, and the subject permutes with MAN4320 at some — check the description, not the number.

courses.reason: Negotiation and Conflict Resolution — 7 institutions. Grievances, investigations and disputes are a large part of the job, and this is the only course that teaches the skill directly.
Principles of Management — 17 institutions, the upper-division management foundation required by most business degrees.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ The lower-division equivalent is MAN2021 Principles of Management at 26 institutions, which is what the state colleges carry. ⚠⚠ Another sector split — check which your target university accepts.

courses.reason: Business Law I — 25 institutions. ⚠ The most consequential course in this list: the judgement calls in HR are legal judgement calls, and getting one wrong creates real liability for your employer.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Universities more often require BUL3130 The Legal Environment of Business (16 institutions) instead. Where your programme offers a dedicated employment law course, take that too.

courses.reason: Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. ⚠⚠ Not a peripheral elective here: psychology is the second largest degree field among working HR staff nationally, and selection, motivation and behaviour are the subject matter of the job.
Interpersonal Communication — 16 institutions. Difficult conversations conducted well are most of what separates an effective HR specialist from a disliked one.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Some colleges satisfy the same requirement with SPC1608 Public Speaking (16 institutions).

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Compensation analysis, turnover metrics and pay-equity review are the analytical half of the field and the route to the better-paid specialisms.
Advanced Business Communication — 28 institutions. Policies, investigation reports and decision letters are written products that may be read years later by a lawyer.
Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. Benefits and compensation are budget lines, and an HR professional who can read a set of accounts argues for headcount more successfully.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. In a dispute, what happened is what the file says happened — and the file is something you wrote.
